name: Tully Mountain
generated_description:
At 2,070 feet, Tully Mountain is a summit in Massachusetts. The Tully Mountain Trail covers 0.7 miles with about 587 feet of elevation gain — a steep, sustained climb. It's rated Easy overall.

The Route

The climbing is spread fairly evenly from start to finish rather than stacked into one steep section. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 0.62, gaining roughly 1,800 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 1,109 feet, the route tops out near 1,696 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 42.45628, -73.18258 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 30 miles southeast of Albany, New York. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Spring through fall is the main season. Conditions change fast in the shoulder months — check a point forecast for the summit, not the nearest town, before you commit.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Yokun Seat, Honwee Mountain and Pine Mountain — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 42.45628, -73.18258 in Massachusetts. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike Tully Mountain?
faqs.answer: Late May through October for snow-free hiking. Check a summit point forecast before you go — conditions up high differ from the trailhead.

faqs.question: How tall is Tully Mountain?
faqs.answer: Tully Mountain stands at 2,070 feet (631 meters) in Massachusetts.
